also: let’s put this off to another time

terms.grammar: verb, irregular; in with the accusative of the new time: in crāstinum, in aliud tempus
evidence: Caes. BC 1.86.2: sī in aliud tempus differētur (Lewis & Short s.v. alius)
Cic. Rep. 2.44: reliqua in crāstinum (differre; Lewis & Short s.v. differō)
Traupman 106: let’s put this off to another time, hanc rem in aliud tempus differāmus
terms.comment: Literally “carry apart”. The new time goes into the accusative with in: in posterum diem, to the next day (Cic. Deiot. 21, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Hanc rem in aliud tempus differāmus.
phrases.english: Let’s put this off to another time.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 106, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
